title: The Neighbour (Chas McIvor)
style: jazz lounge piano bar dry wit spoken word observational 100bpm upright bass brushed snare deadpan baritone male vocal life philosophy absurdist Perth Zimbabwe suburb
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
The neighbour relationship has a specific protocol
You wave across the fence and that's sufficient for the haul
Of any given morning — you don't need the full biography
You need the acknowledging wave and that's the geography

[Pre-Chorus]
My neighbour Frank has been waving at me for twenty-seven years
And I know his dog's name and his car and nothing more appears

[Chorus]
The neighbour knows something I don't know
He knows exactly when I leave for work and which way I go
The neighbour knows the pattern of my bin night without a word
And I know his — and this knowledge is the most that's been transferred
That's my boy

[Verse 2]
There's a point in the neighbour relationship where you've crossed the stage
Of acquaintance and arrived somewhere on a different page
Where you're not quite friends but you'd help if something happened
And the neighbour gap is where the suburb's better character has captained

[Bridge]
The neighbour at our house in Zimbabwe knew everything
About every house on the road and could do the reckoning
Of who was home and who had visitors and why
And that's a different kind of neighbourhood that doesn't apply
In Perth entirely — but nearly

[Outro]
Neighbour knows… more than he says… the wave contains everything…
That's my boy
